segments.title: Opening excerpt: early records and the Ohio Lucky Seven
segments.summary: Steiner introduces the 1961 interview excerpts; Davison recalls the Original Dixieland Jazz Band records and a 1921 dance in Ohio with the Ohio Lucky Seven.

segments.title: Birth in Defiance, Ohio and parents
segments.summary: Davison gives his birthplace, 1906, and his parents' names, Anna Kreps and Edward Davison.

segments.title: Musical family, library home and rowboat rehearsals
segments.summary: His mother and grandmother taught piano but did not encourage him; raised in a Carnegie Library, he practiced cornet, banjo and mandolin along the river, self-taught.

segments.title: First band, the Ohio Lucky Seven, and jazz outside New Orleans
segments.summary: His first band in Defiance was the Ohio Lucky Seven; he argues fine jazz musicians came from places like Indiana, such as Bix.

segments.title: Original Dixieland Jazz Band and New Orleans Rhythm Kings as models
segments.summary: They discuss how Bix and others learned tunes from records by the ODJB and NORK, which started a style.

segments.title: Early jazz records: Ted Lewis and Victor's ensemble-only rule
segments.summary: Davison recalls early Ted Lewis records and says Victor cut out hot solo choruses, requiring all-ensemble playing.

segments.chapter: Cincinnati riverboats and New Orleans players
segments.title: Hearing Fate Marable's band and Pops Foster in Cincinnati
segments.summary: On the Island Queen to Coney Island, Davison heard Fate Marable's riverboat band with Pops Foster and Marable's calliope.

segments.chapter: Cincinnati riverboats and New Orleans players
segments.title: Steve Brown and Phil Spitalny at the Edgewater Beach; tape ends
segments.summary: Asked about New Orleans players, Davison mentions Min Leibrook and Steve Brown, whom he got into Spitalny's band at the Edgewater Beach; Steiner then stops the tape.
